extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent applicants and practitioners (outside counsel, in-house counsel) facing a final rejection from the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Tactical guide describing the options, procedural requirements, and practical constraints available to pursue a U.S. patent application after receipt of a final rejection from the USPTO. Covers amendment, appeal, interviews, AFCP 2.0, RCEs, continuations, abandonment, and strategic considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character of a final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rejection is typically issued during second or subsequent examination of the pending patent application and is intended to close prosecution of the pending patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that a final rejection signals an intent to terminate normal prosecution and that special post-final options (appeal, RCE, AFCP, interview, continuation) are available to continue pursuit of allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory response periods and abandonment consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent applicant will generally have three months or six months time (with extension fee) from the mailing date of the final rejection to send in an appropriate reply. If the applicant fails to respond within the stipulated period, the application will be abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals: the notice of appeal should be filed within a maximum period of six months from the final rejection, unless a shortened period is expressly specified in the office action. Failure to file required documents within stated periods (e.g., appeal brief within two months of notice of appeal) can result in dismissal or abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may respond to the office action by making amendments (e.g., canceling claims or complying with any requirement of form expressly set forth in the office action). An amendment touching the merits may be admitted upon a showing of good and sufficient reasons why the amendment is necessary and was not earlier presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the response to the final office action overcomes the rejections, a notice of allowance will be issued. If the response fails to overcome the rejections, the USPTO will issue an advisory action. Prepare justification for late merit-affecting amendments (good and sufficient reasons).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant whose patent application claims have been rejected twice may appeal the examiner’s decision to the PTAB by filing a notice of appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File the notice of appeal within the maximum six-month period (unless the office action shortens it). After filing the notice of appeal, an appeal brief must be filed within two months from the date of filing the notice of appeal; failure to file the appeal brief will result in the appeal being dismissed. Appeals are appropriate when rejections persist and further examiner reconsideration is unlikely to succeed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may grant one interview to the applicant to place the application in condition for allowance or to resolve issues prior to appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before the interview, present the intended purpose and content briefly and preferably in writing. Interviews will be granted only if the examiner is convinced disposal or clarification for appeal may be accomplished with only nominal further consideration. Interviews that merely restate arguments or propose new limitations requiring more than nominal reconsideration or new search will be denied. Interviews may be held after expiration of any shortened statutory period and before the maximum permitted statutory period of six months without extension. A second or further interview may be granted if it will expedite issues for appeal or disposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: After Final Consideration Pilot 2.0 (AFCP 2.0) request requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To use AFCP 2.0, the applicant should submit a request for consideration under AFCP along with a response that includes an amendment to at least one independent claim; the amendment must not broaden the scope of the independent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one AFCP 2.0 request may be filed in response to an outstanding final rejection. If the amendment necessitates additional search/consideration that cannot be completed within allotted time, the examiner may issue an advisory action. If no additional search is required or it can be completed within time, the examiner will determine if the amendment places the application in condition for allowance; if not, the examiner will contact the applicant and request an interview. AFCP 2.0 has been found effective in advancing prosecution and reducing likelihood of filing an RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Continued Examination (RCE) mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE is a request filed by the applicant for continued prosecution of the application after receiving a final rejection. The RCE should be filed before abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing an RCE withdraws the last office action (final rejection). An RCE may be accompanied by new arguments or amendments. Consider RCE cost and timing relative to other options (e.g., AFCP, appeal, continuation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing a continuation application
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation application has the same disclosure as the pending application but may claim different scope; it undergoes new examination and does not get abandoned when the pending application is abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuation applications allow pursuing claims of varying scope or re-drafting rejected claims. However, if rejected claims from the parent are presented unchanged in the continuation, the first office action on the continuation may itself be a final rejection. Use continuation to preserve prosecution options while pursuing different claim scopes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment as a consequence
rubrics_metrics.description: Not responding within the time set forth in the final office action (or any extended period) will result in abandonment of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abandonment ends prosecution unless revival is later sought under applicable rules (not discussed on this page). Timely evaluation of options and deadlines is critical to avoid inadvertent abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic evaluation: cost and choice of post-final option(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different options after final rejection have differing costs and allow different substantive actions; an applicant must carefully evaluate their prosecution position and choose the option(s) that best serve their interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some options are more expensive than others (e.g., RCEs, continuations, appeals). Consider prospect of allowance, scope you want to pursue, time, examiner likelihood to change position, and whether options like AFCP or interview could cheaply resolve issues before spending more on RCEs or appeals.
